title: Runtime Multiplex Profiling and Cost Anchoring Playbook
author: Marcus Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook codifies how Redwood’s runtime should perform cross-tenant request multiplexing, continuous profiling, and cost-anchoring so teams can safely trade latency for unit-cost while protecting SLOs. It defines guardrails, telemetry requirements, configuration knobs, and an operational rollout checklist for any service implementing multiplexed scheduling (rosetta-runtime, multiplex-proxy, or shard-manager).

Motivation
----------
Multiplexing (concurrent packing of multiple logical requests onto batching windows and shared GPU slices) is one of the highest-impact levers for reducing per-token cost. However, naive multiplexing can cause tail latency amplification, KV cache contention, and unpredictable cost attribution. This playbook provides a standard approach for:
- Profiling and measuring multiplexing benefits and regressions
- Anchoring cost savings to explicit SLO impact budgets
- Operationalizing gradual rollout with automatic rollback triggers

Scope
-----
Applies to: runtime components that perform request collation and kernel sharing, including rosetta-runtime, corridor-batcher, and multiplex-proxy. Excludes: client-side batching in SDKs (see api-standards), storage-only services, and offline batch jobs.

Definitions
-----------
- Multiplexing window: time interval where the runtime groups in-flight requests to form a single kernel/inference batch.
- Cost anchor: a baseline per-token cost estimate for a given workload used to compute realized savings. Anchors are workload- and region-specific.
- Profiling trace: a high-cardinality trace that captures kernel utilization, sequence length distribution, and per-request stall time.

Principles
----------
1. SLO-first: any multiplexing optimization must define the maximum allowable SLO delta (absolute and relative) before activation. Typical default: 99th percentile latency must not degrade by more than 5% absolute or 10% relative.
2. Observable-by-default: profiling traces and derived metrics must be emitted for every enabled tenant at safe sampling rates.
3. Conservative rollout: changes are staged per-tenant via feature flags, canaries, and capacity-limited pilots.
4. Cost transparency: reported savings are tied to anchored baseline and reconciled weekly against billing telemetry.

Guidelines for Profiling and Telemetry
------------------------------------
Emit the following signals (minimum):
- batch_size_distribution.p50/p95/p99 (per-model, per-tenant)
- multiplex_window_ms.p50/p95/p99
- kernel_utilization (GPU SM utilization normalized to batch composition)
- per_request_hold_time_ms (time request waited before execution)
- kv_cache_hit_ratio (tenant-scoped)
- per_token_cost_estimate (based on hardware, kernel, and effective batch size)

Sampling policy:
- Default sampling for production: 1% of requests for full profiling traces, augmented with adaptive burst sampling when tail latencies exceed thresholds.
- For tenants in pilot: 100% profiling traces for first 48 hours, then 10% for the next 14 days.

Alerting baselines (suggested):
- Latency SLI breach: 99th percentile latency exceeds SLO by 10% for 10 minutes.
- Tail amplification: p99 latency increases by >20% compared to baseline within a tenant group after feature toggle.
- Cost regression: per_token_cost_estimate increases by >5% at 1-hour aggregation.

Cost Anchoring and Measurement
-----------------------------
Anchors should be created before any multiplexing change:
1. Baseline run: capture 7-day rolling mean of per_token_cost_estimate and throughput by traffic class.
2. Anchor metadata: model_id, shard_profile, region, tenant_class, workload_signature_hash.
3. Normalization: apply sequence-length normalization to compare different run windows (normalize to median sequence length).
4. Savings computation: weekly_reconciled_savings = (baseline_cost - observed_cost) * normalized_token_count. Reconcile against billing exports to detect attribution gaps.

Operational rollout playbook (step-by-step)
-----------------------------------------
1. Prepare canary bundle
   - Define canary tenants (3–5 tenants representing typical, long-tail, and worst-case sequence lengths).
   - Ensure canary tenants have up-to-date profiling anchors.
2. Deploy in rosetta-runtime behind feature-flag: multiplexing.enabled = off
3. Enable for canary with conservative parameters:
   - multiplex_window_ms: 6ms
   - max_multiplex_batch_size: 4
   - tenant_priority_threshold: 0.2
4. Monitor for 24 hours with high sampling; look for: kv_cache_hit_ratio drop, per_request_hold_time rising, kernel_utilization change.
5. If any of the following triggers fire, immediately rollback for the affected tenant:
   - p99 latency breach > SLO + 10% sustained for 10 minutes
   - per_token_cost_estimate increase > 5% for 30 minutes
   - kv_cache_hit_ratio drop > 8 percentage points
6. Gradually widen rollout over 2–4 weeks, increasing multiplex_window_ms in controlled steps and lowering tenant_priority_threshold.
7. After full rollout, switch to steady-state sampling (1% traces) and weekly cost reconciliation.

Configuration matrix (recommended defaults)
-----------------------------------------
| knob                          | default (pilot) | pilot -> steady state change |
|-------------------------------|-----------------|------------------------------|
| multiplex_window_ms           | 6               | 8 -> 12                      |
| max_multiplex_batch_size      | 4               | 8                            |
| tenant_priority_threshold     | 0.2             | 0.05                         |
| adaptive_backoff_enabled      | true            | true                         |
| profiling_sample_rate         | 100% (canary)   | 1%                          |

Example runtime YAML snippet
----------------------------

runtime:
  multiplexing:
    enabled: true
    window_ms: 8
    max_batch_size: 6
    priority_threshold: 0.1
    adaptive_backoff:
      enabled: true
      p99_latency_trigger_ms: 1200

CLI operations
--------------
- To toggle for a tenant:
  ./infractl runtime feature-flag set --tenant tenant-id --flag multiplexing.enabled --value true
- To inspect live profile samples (debug):
  ./infractl runtime profiles tail --tenant tenant-id --sample 0.1 --filter \"model_id:gemini-large\"

Monitoring and Alerting
----------------------
Define composite alerts that combine latency and cost signals to avoid noisy rollbacks:
- Composite: (p99_latency > SLO * 1.10 for 10m) AND (per_token_cost_estimate increase <= 3%) => page SRE (urgent)
- Composite: (p99_latency > SLO * 1.10 for 10m) AND (per_token_cost_estimate increase > 3%) => automated rollback + page on-call
- Cost-only alert (weekly): realized_savings diverges from billed_savings by >15% => ops-cost-investigation ticket

Testing and Benchmarking
------------------------
- Synthetic fuzz bench: create traffic shapes with sequence-length quantiles {10, 50, 200, 1024} and test multiplexing window sweep (2ms to 20ms).
- Shadow run: route 10% of production traffic to multiplex-enabled cluster with responses discarded but telemetry collected.
- Acceptance criteria: for each workload class, p99 latency <= SLO + 5% and cost reduction >= 6% vs anchor.

Known failure modes and mitigations
----------------------------------
- KV cache churn: mitigate by tenant-aware cache partitioning and soft-lease extension policy.
- Tail amplification: enable adaptive_backoff: decrease multiplex window for affected shard for 10 minutes.
- Attribution drift: reconcile anchors weekly and restore previous anchor if drift unexplained.

Ownership and Review
--------------------
Primary owner: runtime-performance team (runtime-performance@redwood.com).
Review cadence: quarterly or before any cross-shard multiplexing change.
Required reviewers for major changes: Runtime Performance lead, Eng SRE, Observability, Billing.

Rollout sign-off checklist
-------------------------
1. Baseline anchors validated (owner sign-off).
2. Canary tenants identified and consented.
3. Dashboard and alerting created with test annotations.
4. Automation for rollback tested in canary environment.
5. Billing reconciliation ETL configured to surface savings.

Appendix: example dashboard widgets
----------------------------------
- p99 latency by tenant (heatmap)
- multiplex_window_ms histogram (real-time)
- per_token_cost_estimate vs baseline (line chart)
- kernel_utilization stacked by model
